items.title: Control labels overlap move prompts
items.what: In the gameplay screenshots, the white text for 'STANCE' and 'TECHNIQUE' at the bottom of the screen sits directly underneath the directional input glyphs (arrows/triangles).
items.why: It creates visual noise and makes it harder for the player to quickly parse the control scheme during high-intensity combat.
items.how: Increase the vertical padding between the joystick visual assets and the text labels, or move the labels to a dedicated HUD area above the sticks.

items.title: Score HUD lacks sufficient contrast
items.what: The score numbers (e.g., '30' and '0') in the top HUD are rendered in a thin, gold font against a dark, textured background with volumetric light particles.
items.why: In a fast-paced fighting game, players need to glance at the score instantly; the current low-contrast/thin weight makes it difficult to read at a glance.
items.how: Add a subtle dark drop shadow or a semi-transparent dark backing plate behind the score numbers to pop them from the background.

items.title: Techniques menu obscures gameplay context
items.what: The 'TECHNIQUES' overlay screen covers nearly 80% of the vertical viewport, leaving only a tiny sliver of the dojo visible at the top.
items.why: Players often check move lists mid-match; completely obscuring the fighters prevents them from maintaining situational awareness of the opponent's position.
items.how: Convert the Techniques menu into a semi-transparent side-panel or a bottom-sheet that only occupies the lower 40% of the screen.

items.title: Hit sparks compete with character silhouettes
items.what: During the 'IPPON' animation, the bright yellow/white impact sparks are rendered with high bloom, overlapping the fighters' heads and torsos.
items.why: The bloom effect on the impact particles is so strong it washes out the character models, making it hard to see the actual contact point of the strike.
items.how: Reduce the bloom intensity specifically for combat particle effects or use a more localized, less 'glowy' particle sprite for hits.

items.title: Joystick center-point ambiguity
items.what: The 'Stance' and 'Technique' joysticks use a very subtle, low-contrast dot to indicate the neutral center position.
items.why: On a mobile screen, players need a clear visual anchor to know where their thumb is relative to the 'zero' position for precise directional inputs.
items.how: Increase the brightness and size of the center-point dot, or add a subtle ring around the neutral center to provide a clear visual target.
